_comment: What the backend, and the agent that reads its results, are told about this Splunk. Written by a person, not generated.
Start from GET /catalog on soc-mcp-splunk, which enumerates what is really
there. Then add the part enumeration cannot know: what each sourcetype is
for, which field carries which meaning, and what is easy to get wrong.
'roles' is the important part — it maps a meaning to this sourcetype's
field name. The backend searches on it, so a filter gets built on 'srcip'
rather than on a CIM name that does not exist here.
Roles: src_ip dest_ip src_port dest_port user host hash domain url file process service action
Keep it short. It is read on every run that touches Splunk, and every token
here is one taken away from the alert.

main.purpose: The lab estate. FortiGate sample events (recent); one Windows web server, KBTG-Bootcamp, on 24 Dec 2024 16:43-17:58 UTC (Apache access log, Sysmon, Windows event logs); and the corp.local office on 24 Dec 2024 08:00-20:00 UTC: file server FS-01, workstations WS-*, Linux web-02, firewall FGT-01, DNS ns-01. Nothing but the FortiGate samples is recent — a search must reach back to 24 Dec 2024.

access_combined.purpose: Apache access log of the web server. One line per HTTP request.
notes: `clientip` is who made the request. There is no destination field: every event is the one web server.
`status` is the HTTP response code, the only outcome here: 200 served, 403 refused, 404 not there. There is no `action`.
`user` and `ident` are always `-`, and `host` is a label put on at load, not the server's name. Search neither.
Over a million requests in four minutes, nearly all 404 or 403. Count by `status` or `useragent`; to see what worked, exclude 404 and 403.

sysmon.purpose: Sysmon on KBTG-Bootcamp and the corp.local machines. Process creation (EventCode 1) mostly; also process access (10), file create (11), registry set (13), named pipes (17, 18).
notes: No network events (EventCode 3) were collected: there is no IP address in this sourcetype. An address is in access_combined or wineventlog.
`User` is DOMAIN\name, e.g. `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM`; match a bare account name with a wildcard: User="*\\name".
`SHA256` is the bare hash. An MD5 or IMPHASH is only inside `Hashes` (MD5=...,SHA256=...,IMPHASH=...): Hashes="*value*". No SHA1.
Write each backslash of a value twice inside quotes: Image="C:\\Windows\\name.exe". Written once, it matches nothing.
Follow a process to its children with ParentImage or ParentProcessGuid, not ProcessId, which is reused.
EventCode 10 is one process opening another: `SourceImage` opened `TargetImage` with the rights in `GrantedAccess` (0x1FFFFF is full access). It has no `Image` or `User`; its account is `SourceUser`.
`host` is a load label; the machine is `Computer`, a full name like WS-12.corp.local: Computer="WS-12*".
Most events are the Splunk forwarder's own helpers (Image under SplunkUniversalForwarder). Exclude them to see the rest.

wineventlog.purpose: Windows Security, System and Application event logs of KBTG-Bootcamp and FS-01: logons (4624, 4625 failed, 4634, 4672, 4776), services (7036, 7045).
notes: `Account_Name` has two values in a 4624 and a 4625: who asked for the logon (often `-`), then the account logged on or tried. Take the second: mvindex(Account_Name, -1). A 4776 names the account in `Logon_Account` instead.
A 4625 is a failed logon. `Sub_Status` says why: 0xC0000064 no such account, 0xC000006A wrong password, 0xC0000234 locked out.
`Source_Network_Address` is `-` for a local logon. Logon_Type 3 is over the network, 5 is a service.
`ComputerName` is the machine that wrote the event; `Workstation_Name` is the remote client and is often empty.
A new service is EventCode 7045: `Service_Name` and `Service_File_Name`. 7036 is only a service changing state.
Field names are the labels in the message with spaces as underscores. EventID, src_ip and dest do not exist here.

fortigate.purpose: FortiGate traffic and UTM events. One line per session or detection.
notes: `host` is the syslog forwarder that shipped the event, NOT the machine the alert is about. Use `srcip`.
`devname` is the firewall appliance, not an endpoint.
action values: accept, deny, blocked, close. `deny` and `blocked` mean the firewall stopped it — the connection did not complete.
type=traffic is a session; type=utm carries virus/IPS detections and adds `virus` and `filename`.
Internal addresses are 10.10.0.0/16 (dstcountry=Reserved). `sentbyte`/`rcvdbyte` are bytes per session.
These logs are NOT CIM-normalised: src_ip, dest_ip, dvc and src do not exist here.

linux_secure.purpose: Authentication log (/var/log/secure) of the Linux web server web-02: sshd logins and sudo.
notes: sshd: `action` is Failed or Accepted, `auth_method` password or publickey, `user` the account tried (also invalid ones).
sudo: `user` ran `command` as `target_user`. A sudo line has no `src`.
`host` is the server itself here (web-02).

bind_query.purpose: BIND query log of the internal DNS server ns-01 (10.10.1.53). One line per DNS query.
notes: `src` is the client that asked; `query` the full name asked for; `record_type` A, AAAA, TXT, SRV...
No answers or response codes are logged — only the questions.
To group by domain, cut `query` to its last two labels: mvjoin(mvindex(split(query, "."), -2, -1), ".").
